title: A week in Nashville
summary: Seven days of hot chicken and meat-and-threes, honky-tonks and the Opry, songwriter nights, and green trails just outside town.
author: Nate Bird

places.name: The Hermitage Hotel
places.notes: Nashville's grand 1910 hotel. Even the Art Deco men's room is a sight.

places.name: The Union Station Nashville Yards
places.notes: A 1900 railroad station with a stained glass vaulted lobby, at the quiet end of Broadway.

places.name: Noelle
places.notes: A 1930s building with a rooftop bar, two blocks from the honky-tonks but calmer.

places.name: Graduate Nashville
places.notes: A playful hotel near Vanderbilt, with a rooftop bar themed on Dolly Parton.

places.name: Prince's Hot Chicken Shack
places.notes: The family that invented Nashville hot chicken. Start at mild. Really.

places.name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken
places.notes: The busiest hot chicken in town, with good sides. Go mid-afternoon to skip the line.

places.name: Bolton's Spicy Chicken & Fish
places.notes: Fiery chicken and whiting in a small East Nashville shack. Ask for it hot only if you mean it.

places.name: Arnold's Country Kitchen
places.notes: The classic meat-and-three, weekday lunch only. Roast beef, greens and chess pie.

places.name: Loveless Cafe
places.notes: Biscuits and preserves at an old motel café near the Natchez Trace. Book or arrive early.

places.name: Pancake Pantry
places.notes: Pancakes by the stack since 1961, with a line down the block on weekends.

places.name: Biscuit Love
places.notes: Biscuits all ways. The bonuts, fried biscuit doughnuts, are the thing.

places.name: Martin's Bar-B-Que Joint
places.notes: Whole-hog West Tennessee barbecue with a big beer garden upstairs.

places.name: Husk
places.notes: Southern-only ingredients in an 1880s mansion. The burger at lunch is a bargain.

places.name: Rolf and Daughters
places.notes: Handmade pastas in an old Germantown factory. One of the city's best dinners.

places.name: Mas Tacos Por Favor
places.notes: Cheap, excellent tacos and chicken tortilla soup in East Nashville. Cash only.

places.name: Barista Parlor
places.notes: Careful coffee in an old auto garage. Order a biscuit sandwich with it.

places.name: The Patterson House
places.notes: A dark speakeasy-style cocktail bar. Expect a short wait for a seat.

places.name: Robert's Western World
places.notes: The real honky-tonk on Broadway. Order the Recession Special and listen to the house band.

places.name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
places.notes: The purple-fronted bar where Willie Nelson got his first songwriting job. Live music from 10 a.m.

places.name: The Station Inn
places.notes: Bluegrass most nights since 1974. Sunday night is the open jam.

places.name: Ryman Auditorium
places.address: 116 Rep. John Lewis Way N, Nashville, TN 37219
places.notes: The Mother Church of Country Music. Take the daytime tour, then come back for a show.

places.name: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
places.address: 222 Rep. John Lewis Way S, Nashville, TN 37203
places.notes: Elvis's gold Cadillac and the history of country. Add the RCA Studio B tour here.

places.name: Johnny Cash Museum
places.notes: A small, packed museum of the Man in Black. Patsy Cline's museum is upstairs.

places.name: National Museum of African American Music
places.notes: Gospel, blues, jazz and hip-hop in one interactive museum. Make your own track.

places.name: Frist Art Museum
places.notes: Changing exhibitions in a 1934 Art Deco post office.

places.name: Grand Ole Opry
places.notes: The longest-running radio show in America. Buy tickets for a Friday or Saturday show.

places.name: The Bluebird Cafe
places.notes: Songwriters playing their hits in the round, in a 90-seat room. Tickets go fast online.

places.name: The Parthenon
places.notes: A full-size copy of the Athens Parthenon, with a 42-foot gilded Athena inside.

places.name: Tennessee State Capitol
places.address: 600 Dr. Martin L King Jr Blvd, Nashville, TN 37243
places.notes: An 1859 Greek Revival capitol on a hill. Free guided tours on weekdays.

places.name: The Hermitage
places.notes: Andrew Jackson's plantation, told with the lives of the people enslaved there.

places.name: Belle Meade Historic Site & Winery
places.notes: A Greek Revival plantation and thoroughbred farm, with a wine tasting after the tour.

places.name: Centennial Park
places.notes: Lawns and a lake around the Parthenon. Free concerts and dance on summer evenings.

places.name: Cheekwood Estate & Gardens
places.notes: A 1920s mansion and 55 acres of gardens. Best in spring and during the holiday lights.

places.name: John Seigenthaler Pedestrian Bridge
places.address: John Seigenthaler Pedestrian Bridge, Nashville, TN 37201
places.notes: Walk across the Cumberland River for the best skyline view in town, especially at night.

places.name: Bicentennial Capitol Mall State Park
places.notes: A long state history walk below the Capitol, next to the Nashville Farmers' Market.

places.name: Shelby Bottoms Greenway
places.notes: Flat river trails through wetlands and woods. Rent a bike and ride to the Cumberland.

places.name: Radnor Lake State Park
places.notes: A quiet lake with deer, owls and herons, fifteen minutes from downtown.

places.name: Warner Parks
places.notes: Wooded hills, stone gates and a long scenic drive. Climb the Allée steps at the main entrance.
